description:
**KCB 0.5.0's capability-versioning fold — V-1 through V-8 — has no tasklist anywhere.** Same shape as the federation fold, one phase over: `54`, `55` and `56` merged and produced eight findings, and the specs still describe the pre-finding design. An 18-repo audit on 2026-08-25 confirmed nothing in any repo owns it.

**KCB is the most-implemented plane and the most-gated spec.** agora's `registry/`, `grants/` and both routers are built against it, and it carries three separate counts holding it at Candidate. So the divergence here is not theoretical: real routing code is running against a contract whose known gaps are unwritten.

**Capability versioning is where a fabric quietly breaks.** A provider advertises a capability, a consumer resolves it, and the two disagree about what version means — that failure surfaces as a runtime mismatch far from its cause. koine `ADR-0001` puts discovery on the bus with the registry returning ADDRESSES rather than proxying, so version negotiation happens peer to peer with no hub to arbitrate. Whatever V-1…V-8 found about that has to end up in the clause, because there is no central component that could compensate for a vague one.

**Same reactive discipline as `85`.** Fold each break to the extent it forces and no further; close the ones already covered or found to be scenario errors, with reasoning. Eight findings do not obligate eight clauses.

**And check it against `85`.** Federation and capability versioning meet: a capability advertised across an authority boundary is both. The two folds must not contradict each other, and if they conflict, that conflict is itself a finding worth an ADR rather than a quiet reconciliation in one of them.
warmup: python3 -c "import json,glob;[print(f.split('/')[-1], json.load(open(f)).get('mergedToMain')) for f in sorted(glob.glob('tasks/chief/completed/5[456]-*.json'))]"

userStories.title: Each of the eight findings gets a disposition
acceptanceCriteria: V-1 through V-8 are each classified FOLD, CLOSE (already covered, or the finding was wrong — with reasoning) or DEFER (with the future break that would force it).
Each disposition names the spec section it lands in, and whether it also touches the schema twin or the relation registry.
The three counts currently holding KCB at Candidate are identified and mapped against these findings, so it is clear which of them this fold clears and which it does not.
Table only — no clause changes in this story.
userStories.notes: docs/reference/capability-versioning-fold-dispositions.md: all 8 findings dispositioned (7 FOLD incl. 3 splits, 1 CLOSE, 2 DEFER-D/E + 1 rejected-on-record). Each names its KCB section; no schema twin and no registry file moves (V-2's shape-registry route rejected on federation grounds). Counts: the tasklist said three, the spec now carries FIVE — all five enumerated and mapped; this fold clears NONE, count (ii) changes shape only. No clause or version touched. check-doc-integrity.mjs: OK, 1226 links, 3 status tables match; check-tasklist-categories.mjs: OK.

userStories.title: The folds land, and version negotiation is unambiguous
acceptanceCriteria: Each FOLD is applied minimally to the named section, with a version bump, a reconsidered Status, and a changelog entry citing the V-id.

The resulting clause is specific enough that two independent implementations negotiate the same way without consulting each other. Under ADR-0001 the registry returns an address and peers dial directly — there is no hub to reconcile a disagreement, so a clause that leaves room for interpretation produces a runtime mismatch far from its cause.
A test or conformance case demonstrates the negotiated behaviour rather than only asserting the prose. Where KCS can encode it, encode it.
Schema twins updated where the shape moved; relation registry additions are new immutable names, never in-place signature edits.
userStories.notes: KCB 0.4.9 -> 0.5.0 (minor), Candidate. V-1..V-7 folded, V-8 closed: new §2.4 (transport binding, V-4), new §4.4 (version operand + granted major in the token + refuse-for-want-of-one, V-5; quoted_cost + quote-mismatch refusal, V-1), §2.1+§7.1 (payload_schema_id + bare-shape-is-no-cross-check, V-2; shape registry rejected on the record), §7.1 step 5 (canonicalization rule id, absent=kcb1, no published digest moves, V-3), §7.3c (floor per axis, V-6), §7.3g (successor/deprecated/removal frames on §4.2d's existing channel, V-7), plus §5/§6/§4.1/§7.2 cross-refs. §2.2's standalone manifest REMOVED at 0.5.0 (declared obligation now due, not a fold); §2.3's window untouched at 0.6.0. Conformance case: scenarios/e2e-live-schema-mutation.md gains F1-F13, the assertion set the KCS encoding must grow (DR-7: re-running today's encoding proves nothing); no scenario file added, so downstream set-equality is unaffected. Schema twins: none moved (no twin models the KCB card extension) — vacuous. Registry: none moved (V-2's registry route rejected). Verification: node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs OK (52 files, 1249 links, 3 status tables match headers); check-schemas.mjs OK; check-registry.mjs OK; check-tasklist-categories.mjs OK; .chief/verify.sh green (verify-test: 30 passed, 0 failed).

userStories.title: This fold and the federation fold agree
acceptanceCriteria: The result is read against `85-fold-the-federation-breaks`. A capability advertised across an authority boundary is governed by both, and the two must not specify different behaviour for it.

Any conflict is raised as an ADR rather than resolved silently inside one of the folds. A contradiction between two folds is a design finding about the fabric, and burying it in whichever fold merges second is how it becomes invisible.

agora's registry and grants are checked against the folded clause and any divergence is reported as an agora finding. koine specifies and agora implements — but a fold that the reference implementation already contradicts should be known before it ships, not after.
State whether KCB is now promotable. It is the most-implemented plane in the fabric and the answer matters to both organizations reading it.
